title: France's Sesterce plans $11 billion AI investment in Finland
source_used: Reuters wire text, read on Yahoo Finance (copy site)
key_facts: French AI infrastructure group Sesterce said on Thursday 8 Oct 2026 it plans to develop a data centre site in Finland costing more than €10 billion ($11.21 billion).
The first phase, with works planned to start in 2026, will have capacity of 200 megawatts; capacity is expected to rise to 600 MW in the second phase.
The company says it already has an anchor customer for the project, which is not named in the report.
The site is at Jamsa in central Finland, on the former paper mill site that closed in 2021.
Over the longer term Sesterce aims to build more than 1 gigawatt of AI capacity in Finland, on existing industrial sites and in line with market demand.
The project is described as the latest in a series of foreign technology investments in Finland.
quote_evidence: French AI infrastructure group Sesterce said on Thursday it plans to develop a data centre site in Finland costing more than €10 billion ($11.21 billion), the latest in a series of foreign technology investments in the Nordic country.
The company said it already has an anchor customer for the project, which will be built in Jamsa in central Finland at the site of a former paper mill that closed in 2021.
why_it_matters_hint: A large planned AI data centre in Finland, with power demand of 200 MW rising to 600 MW, on a former industrial site.
